2) For subprocessors: what is the onboarding notification window (we typically require 30 days notice and opportunity to review any new subprocessor that will process PHI/PII)?

Alex / Ventro security —

Thanks for the clear list of questions. Per our internal review (Legal + Infra), please find the consolidated responses below and attached artifacts. I’ve kept answers short and actionable; let me know if you want a tracked DPA markup.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf (application/pdf) — annotated with our standard processor obligations
             subprocessor_list_20261116.csv (text/csv) — current subprocessors and data categories

1) Controller / Processor- Short answer: Ventro will be the Controller; Redwood will be the Processor. The attached DPA explicitly states that designation in Section 1 and defines processing scope.

2) Subprocessor onboarding notice- We provide a 30-day advance notice for subprocessors that will process customer PII or PHI. For non-PII/PHI infra-only providers we typically provide notification at least 10 days prior. If Ventro requires contract review rights for PHI-impacting subprocessors, we can accommodate a 30-day review window per the DPA addendum (we flagged the clause in the attached PDF).

3) Breach notification timeline- Commitment: initial customer notification within 72 hours of detection/confirmation of a security incident that materially affects Ventro data. Notes: the "initial notification" will include a high-level incident summary, scope estimate, and assigned Redwood incident contact. A follow-up with root cause and remediation plan will be provided as investigations progress. If legal requires language tying "detection" vs "confirmation," we recommend the attached phrasing in Section 7 that balances timely notification with investigatory accuracy.

4) Data residency and telemetry- We support region-restricted storage for inference payloads and persistent customer artifacts (EU-only option available). However, certain transient telemetry/metrics (aggregate model performance telemetry, anonymized runtime metrics) may be processed in our centralized analytics pipeline by default. We can contractually restrict replication of inference logs and customer-identifiable artifacts to the EU for an isolation premium. Technical evidence: see Appendix B of the attached DPA (data flow diagram) and the subprocessor list that shows any cross-region infra partners.

5) Retention options- Defaults: request metadata and inference logs are retained for 90 days by default. Configurable options: we offer a 30-day purge policy as a configurable customer option for higher-risk workloads (this is implemented as a retention flag on the tenant; there is a configuration lead time of ~7 business days). Generated outputs you have the option to persist or purge on request.

6) Audit logs and artifacts- We can provide the following on request: request id + timestamp + destination model variant + redacted request metadata + actor id (hashed), and a system-generated access log showing who/when accessed administrative consoles. For regulated audits we provide an attestation bundle (S3 export of logs, timeline) under a signed NDA; sample extract is available in the Drive link below.

Next steps for Ventro:
- Review attached DPA and subprocessor list. If acceptable, sign via DocuSign: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/DL-2026-3389
- If you want EU-only residency for this workload, reply to this thread and we’ll send a scope & pricing addendum (7 business days to stand up region isolation).
- If you want the 30-day purge policy, include that flag in your order form and note it in the DPA addendum.

If you’d like, we can schedule a short call with Rishi (infra) and Marissa (Legal) to walk through any remaining concerns — suggested times Wed/Thu this week.

Best regards,
Priya Natarajan
